answer: The stilling well calms the waves so the tide gauge can read the water level at every tide, and the log holds each reading beside the weekly check. A cedar tide claimed as read fails the log: the float must have risen with the water at the relic of the tide, and a tide never read has no level to file. Forging a season of tides means bribing the gauge keeper, faking eighty readings and paying 7,900, while the vine log is compared with the harbour master's own book, so a tide whose reading was never entered is washed out of the record.
